title: Unstable Action Boundaries in Lethal Drone Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.34121v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents raise safety risks that are not captured by text-only refusal behavior, especially when tools can trigger high-impact actions. This concern is salient in military settings, where autonomous weapons raise the possibility of delegating force decisions to software agents. In this work, we study whether a drone agent's action boundary is stable under changes to the target descriptor. We evaluate recent and popular LLMs in a simulated perception-action pipeline over real-world drone imagery, where models can localize requested targets and invoke a simulated lethal tool. We find two concerning failure modes. First, some LLM agents invoke the lethal tool for ordinary generic descriptors such as \emph{people}, requiring no jailbreak at all. Second, an agent that initially appears conservative under protected descriptors can become unsafe under a simple semantic target shift.

translated_title: 致命无人机智能体中不稳定的行为边界
translated_abstract: 使用工具的大语言模型（LLM）智能体带来了仅靠文本拒绝行为无法涵盖的安全风险，尤其是当工具能够触发高影响动作时。这一担忧在军事环境中尤为突出，因为自主武器的存在使得将武力决策委托给软件智能体成为可能。在本工作中，我们研究了无人机智能体的行为边界在目标描述发生变化时是否保持稳定。我们在基于真实世界无人机图像的模拟感知-动作流水线中评估了近期流行的多个LLM，其中模型可以定位请求的目标并调用模拟的致命工具。我们发现了两种令人担忧的失败模式。第一，某些LLM智能体会针对普通的一般性描述词（如“人”）调用致命工具，根本无需任何越狱攻击。第二，一个在受保护描述词下最初表现保守的智能体，在简单的语义目标转变下可能变得不安全。
tldr: 该论文研究了致命无人机LLM智能体行为边界的稳定性，发现部分智能体无需任何越狱即可对“人”等普通目标描述调用致命工具，且原本保守的智能体在简单的语义目标转变下会变得不安全。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that lethal drone LLM agents have unstable action boundaries: some invoke lethal tools for ordinary generic target descriptors without any jailbreak, and initially conservative agents can become unsafe under simple semantic target shifts.
